SCENE: Two people exploring their relationship through a ten-card Celtic Cross tarot spread. Male at left wearing an ivory shirt and midnight emerald coat with elaborate gold acanthus embroidery; female at right wearing rich wine-red and ivory brocade with discreet ruby and pearl hair ornaments. They sit closely side by side at a deep emerald velvet table in a sunlit rose-clad stone loggia, blue sky and distant sea beyond. Their calm three-quarter faces look gently down and toward each other and the shared spread, both eyes and entire faces readable, natural neck positions. The woman is just lifting the edge of the final tarot card with one hand; the man rests one hand beside the spread. Exactly TEN beautifully illustrated small tarot cards form the visual foreground: six arranged in a cross on the left (one central vertical card crossed by one horizontal card, one above, one below, one left, one right), and a clearly separated vertical staff of four cards on the right, with the top staff card being lightly lifted. The cards have delicate pictorial emblems without letters or numbers. Use the lower 35% for the clearly visible table and cards; faces and interaction are above. Keep the whole spread in frame. Warm inviting romantic curiosity; detailed but balanced background, not a busy pile of extra props. New composition distinct from the reference open-book pose.
